title: Submit Zedu to 3-5 relevant EdTech awards programmes and track deadlines, by Fri 4 Dec

acceptedWorkstreams.title: Enter one award end-to-end as the pilot, then batch the rest with the same pack

Tasks: pilot entry (other), pack revision and batch entries (content).

acceptedWorkstreams.title: Long-list 15 programmes, enter the best 3-5, with a pack built only from verified numbers
acceptedWorkstreams.description: Research about 15 awards that fit African EdTech or cohort-learning software, checking each one's official page for open deadline, eligibility, fee and published judging criteria, with a yes or no reason for each. Pick 3-5 that are still open and fit. Build one reusable pack: origin story, product screenshots, press contact and only metrics the team confirms. Don't reuse the homepage numbers (98% satisfaction, 3x faster, 40% less admin) until the claims-audit goal sources them. Then submit and track the dates. Tasks: long list with criteria (research), submission pack (content), submissions and deadline tracker (other).

acceptedWorkstreams.title: Shortlist only awards with published criteria and open deadlines, then reuse one pack
acceptedWorkstreams.description:
Award entries take time, so this approach filters hard before writing anything.
Tasks, each finishable:
1. Research (research): list every EdTech, African tech and startup award found, with the official link, who may enter, the published judging criteria, the entry fee, and a deadline checked on the official page with the date. Each gets a yes or no reason, and only programmes whose criteria and open deadline can be seen on the page qualify.
2. Submission pack (content): an origin story (from public facts and team-supplied details only), a 150-word and a 300-word product description, current screenshots, a press contact placeholder, and a metrics section that contains only numbers the team confirms in writing. Unconfirmed numbers are left out, as the goal requires.
3. Tailored entries (press): adapt the pack to the 3-5 chosen programmes, answering each one's published criteria point by point.
4. Tracker (other): one sheet with programme, deadline, status, and result date.
Nothing is submitted without the goal owner's approval.

upvotes.reason: Filtering to awards with visible criteria and a deadline checked on the official page before writing anything is the right way to avoid wasted entries.
Filtering by published criteria and open deadlines first stops entries being written for programmes that are closed or would reject Zedu, which saves the team's limited time.

It filters awards by official eligibility, judging criteria, fees and open dates before spending time on entries, and it keeps unconfirmed metrics out of the pack. That makes a realistic, reviewable PR opportunity.

Filtering on open deadlines first matters: when I checked EdTech Breakthrough on 22 Oct 2026 for the directories research, its page said 'submit your entry online by March 21, 2026', so the current round has already closed. A shortlist without checked deadlines would waste entry work.
Filters hard on published criteria and open deadlines before writing anything, and keeps unconfirmed numbers out of the pack, as the goal requires.
